title: Driver wins $76 after ALPR led to bogus traffic stop, drug searches
gist: A Texas federal jury awarded Alek Schott a symbolic $76 against Bexar County after an ALPR-derived tip via a law-enforcement WhatsApp group led to a pretextual stop and 76-minute search. Critics say the case shows growing scrutiny of AI-powered plate readers like Flock Safety's.

insights.claim: A federal jury in Texas found for plaintiff Alek Schott against Bexar County, awarding the $76 he requested, one dollar per minute detained.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: Establishes jury-level liability for ALPR-triggered pretextual stops.
insights.locator: Late last month, plaintiff Alek Schott

insights.claim: The deputy admitted the 'lane drifting' reason was bogus; the real trigger was a WhatsApp tip from a fusion-center contact with near real-time ALPR access who flagged a 'one-day turnaround' trip.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: Shows how ALPR pattern-flagging feeds informal, unaccountable policing channels, a liability vector for vendors and agencies.
insights.locator: The real reason for the stop

insights.claim: The Institute for Justice says dashcam showed no lane drift and the drug dog handler signaled the dog before its alert; a 76-minute search found nothing.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: Evidence quality undermines interdiction practices built on ALPR tips.
insights.locator: According to the Institute for Justice

insights.claim: The Institute for Justice will seek an injunction barring Bexar County from using baseless traffic stops for warrantless searches and work to enforce the precedent statewide.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: Possible injunctions could constrain how police use ALPR data across Texas.

insights.claim: The Bexar County Sheriff's Office touts its use of Flock Safety cameras.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: Flock's customers are increasingly exposed to litigation tied to ALPR use.

insights.claim: CDT's Jake Laperruque says ALPR scrutiny is increasing and AI tech sold with 'pie-in-the-sky' public safety promises faces a tough reality check.
insights.speaker: Jake Laperruque
insights.so_what: Rising regulatory and reputational risk for ALPR vendors like Flock.
insights.quote: AI tech that vendors sell with pie-in-the-sky promises to improve public safety often face a tough reality check

insights.claim: Laperruque argues that without guardrails, ALPRs endanger civil liberties and public safety through improper stops and officers abusing the tech to stalk.
insights.speaker: Jake Laperruque
insights.so_what: Supports momentum for ALPR usage regulation.
